# Results

## Free generation selects packages, not wrappers

Amplifying frozen dual-effect / content-supporting features on 20
held-out prompts moves article preference toward `an` on every prompt,
but almost never preserves content. @tbl-packaging summarizes the
clincher and selection-criterion ablation (S1). Wrapper-like repairs
are at chance zero; trajectory-like package switches dominate; illicit
`an`+consonant mismatches stay at zero. Qualitative twins include
`a pilot`\(\rightarrow\)`an aviator` and
`a lawyer`\(\rightarrow\)`an attorney`.

| Condition | \(N\) | Art.\(\rightarrow\)`an` | Content preserved | Class shift | Wrapper | Trajectory | Twin match |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| S1 amplify \(5\times\) | 20 | 1.00 | 0.05 | 0.95 | 0.00 | 0.95 | 0.35 |
| S1 matched control | 20 | 0.70 | 1.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 |
| S3 amplify \(5\times\) | 20 | 0.70 | 0.95 | 0.05 | 0.00 | 0.05 | 0.00 |

: Free-generation packaging versus wrapper metrics (held-out occupations).
S1 is dual-effect; S3 is content-ish. Controls are activation-matched.
{#tbl-packaging}

An earlier frozen LoF pair that repaired the source
`a ophthalmologist`\(\rightarrow\)`an ophthalmologist` likewise failed as
a content-preserving transfer: on held-out data it flipped many expected-`a`
controls to `an` and changed content words on 37/107 prompts, with
**zero** grammar-only repairs that kept the noun fixed
(@fig-generalization).

![Held-out frozen-pair transfer changes articles and content together rather than repairing grammar alone.](docs/collaborator-report/figures/figure3_generalization.png){#fig-generalization width=90%}

## Pasting native \(b\) restores native \(c\)

Under selective article-step intervention with clamps **off** at the noun
step, free S1 amplify remains trajectory-like (\(\approx 95\%\)), but
forcing the native article yields content preservation \(\approx 1.0\):
e.g., free `an aviator` becomes `a pilot` after pasting `a`
(@fig-force-native). This isolates a real \(b\to c\) edge. It
does **not** yet refute independent \(C\to c\), because content
clamps were absent at \(c\).

![Free dual-effect intervention switches packages; pasting the native article restores the native noun.](docs/collaborator-report/figures/figure8_selective_force_native.png){#fig-force-native width=90%}

## Fixed \(b\), content on at \(c\): within-class null

@tbl-fixed-b reports the corrected assay. Across eight occupation
families, S3 amplify/zero, hint-contrast features, and controls yield
**zero** within-class noun switches under fixed native \(b\) with clamps
kept on at \(P\). Same-class noun logits remain \(\approx 5\) below the
source noun. Protocol smoke tests confirm content-on versus content-off
differ at the logit level, so the assay is not collapsing by
construction. S2 (article-ish) still moves article logits under
paste-native while content stays native---a licensing handle compatible
with H2, not a modular content dial.

| Condition | \(c\to c\) | Content \(\Delta\) | Match same-class | Mean \(\Delta\)(same$-$src) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Baseline | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | \(-4.90\) |
| S3 amp \(5\times\) / \(8\times\) / zero | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | \(\approx -4.9\) |
| Hint-contrast amp \(5\times\) | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | \(-4.91\) |
| Control amp \(5\times\) | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | \(-4.92\) |

: Fixed-\(b\), content-on-at-\(c\) within-class rates (8 families).
{#tbl-fixed-b}

![Corrected fixed-\(b\) assay: binary within-class outcomes are all zero; same-class nouns stay ~5 logits below source.](docs/collaborator-report/figures/figure9_fixed_b_content_on.png){#fig-fixed-b width=80%}

## Per-noun sparse features and residual directions also null

A modular defender might blame the wrong sparse objects. We therefore
(i)~select Latent-Planning-style per-example features for each
same-class target (positive target attribution, low article attribution;
plus target$-$source contrast) and (ii)~steer a dense MLP-in residual
direction toward the same-class noun. Both use the same fixed-\(b\),
content-on schedule on three twin families (@tbl-escape).

| Handle | Best \(c\to c\) | Best \(\Delta\Delta\)(same$-$src) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Per-noun LP-target / contrast (amp \(5\times\)--\(8\times\)) | 0.00 | \(+0.29\) |
| Residual content steer \(\alpha=1\)--\(8\) | 0.00 | \(\approx 0.08\) |
| Residual random control \(\alpha=1\)--\(8\) | 0.00 | \(\approx 0.15\) |

: Escape-hatch assays under fixed \(b\). Neither per-noun sparse selection
nor residual MLP-in steering opens a within-class dial; residual content
steering does not beat random controls.
{#tbl-escape}

Every force-on continuation remained on the baseline noun
(`pilot`/`lawyer`/`psychologist`). @fig-residual shows the residual
null; the per-noun sparse null is qualitatively identical.

![Dense residual (MLP-in) content steering under fixed \(b\): within-class outcomes remain zero for content and random directions.](docs/collaborator-report/figures/figure11_residual_fixed_b.png){#fig-residual width=95%}
